notes: §1985:VII.4.4.3 SR2: "The AT END phrase must be specified if no applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is specified for file-name-1". The 1985 text defines neither "applicable" nor "appropriate", and two final adjudications read it opposite ways (2026-11-12, kb/Work PB5413 amendment 1: reading A, a mode procedure is applicable to a statement of any file that can be open in that mode; 2026-11-14, op-20261114/held-adjudicated.json q1: reading B, only a mode in which the statement's condition can arise). So it is implementor latitude, and WiseOwl COBOL takes reading A as a DOCUMENTED LATITUDE CHOICE (kb/Work PB5591; docs/CONFORMANCE.md 3.5; docs/FILES_DESIGN.md D31(a)): reading B would refuse CCVS-85 SQ148A, GnuCOBOL 3.2 -std=cobol85 enforces none of the mandatory-phrase rules and so does not decide, and rejecting legal source is the worse harm. ExceptionPhraseRequirement.HasApplicableUse implements it: a declarative naming the file, or one for an open mode the file can be open in (EXTEND only for a file that can be opened EXTEND, kb/Work PB5413), refuses COBOL6826 otherwise. The witness (pb5591_seq_read_mode_use_excuses_at_end_85) runs at --std 85: the statement with no phrase is accepted under the one mode declarative, and at run time the procedure takes the logic-error status the statement raises in that mode (47, 48 or 49), matching the expectation derived from the text. The adjudication's probe (refute-rs-02/p/t1.cob (ON OUTPUT only) and t2.cob (ON EXTEND only)) observed: t1 re-run this session: compiles, AFTER 47, exit 0 (no data file, OPEN failed); refuter saw AFTER 46 with the file present; no procedure ran; under reading A that is the conforming result. Previous verdict: PARTIAL, held on reading B. Recorded 2026-11-14 by records-85-held from the final held-row adjudication (op-20261114/held-adjudicated.json).

next.reason: §1985:VII.4.4.3 SR2: 'The AT END phrase must be specified if no applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is specified for file-name-1' (a compile-time refusal of a sequential READ). 2023 has no READ syntax rule requiring AT END (§2023:14.9.30.3) and states the refused case: §2023:14.9.30.4 GR24 d): 'If the AT END phrase is not specified in the input-output statement, any applicable at end exception processing statements are executed. If there are no applicable at end exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the READ statement'. This record's own text names AT END only (the 1985 sequential READ has no INVALID KEY phrase), so 'to' holds the at end rule and neither §2023:9.1.14 rule. Words that differ: 1985 'must be specified'; 2023 'not specified ... there are no applicable ... exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end'. A statement 1985 refuses is accepted by 2023 with a stated run-time effect: a lifted refusal, so CHANGED (kb/Work PB5021), not REMOVED.
